clue.text: Judge taking tea-break after. Times puzzle

indicators.note: after places the shuffled tea behind the scrambled Times
to puzzle is to baffle or jumble, so the word Times is scrambled
the tea is broken up, so its three letters are shuffled into a new order

explanation.surface: Someone taking a tea break before tackling the Times crossword.
explanation.walkthrough: 'puzzle' turns TIMES into ESTIM; 'break' turns TEA into ATE; 'after' puts ATE behind ESTIM. The full stop after 'after' is an OCR speck: the page has none.
explanation.definitionFit: To judge a quantity roughly is to estimate it, a verb synonym.

clue.text: North-European school-head taken in by a schoolboy

indicators.note: taken in by puts the head letter inside the pupil

parts.note: an Etonian is a pupil at Eton College, the English public school

indicators.note: the head of the word school is its first letter

explanation.surface: A Baltic headmaster deceived by one of his pupils.
explanation.walkthrough: 'school-head' gives S, which 'taken in by' places inside ETONIAN, a boy at Eton, a famous English boarding school.
explanation.definitionFit: A native of the Baltic state Tallinn is capital of is a northern European.

parts.note: reads like an outdated audio device; really an old-time official who shouted news in the streets

explanation.surface: An old-fashioned audio speaker going out of use.
explanation.definitionFit: Before newspapers, a town official rang a bell and proclaimed announcements loudly in public.

parts.note: reads like a man with well-regarded connections; really the mythical king whose touch turned things to gold

explanation.surface: A man whose network of contacts was highly prized.
explanation.walkthrough: The comma matters: what he touched became precious, not his acquaintances.
explanation.definitionFit: The Phrygian king of Greek myth was granted a golden touch, making all he handled precious.

clue.text: When one may go to pot

definitions.text: When one may go to pot

parts.words: When one may go to pot
parts.note: reads like a time of ruin or decline; really the hour when leaves are put in the pot to brew

explanation.surface: The moment someone lets things go to ruin.
explanation.definitionFit: The afternoon meal is when leaves are put into a pot to brew, a British custom.

clue.text: Put in plain words, fish in the river

indicators.note: in places the fish inside the river's name

parts.note: the Dee is a British river, a crossword favourite
the cod is a common food fish

explanation.surface: An instruction to describe plainly the fish in the river.
explanation.walkthrough: 'in' puts COD inside DEE, a river in Scotland and another on the England–Wales border.
explanation.definitionFit: Decoding a coded message renders it in ordinary readable language.

parts.note: reads like schoolchildren grumbling about homework; really the ailment of tired parts of the eye

explanation.surface: Schoolchildren moaning about too much work.
explanation.definitionFit: Pupils are the dark centres of the eyes, and tiring them causes visual fatigue.

clue.text: On active service one's stationed in the desert

parts.note: OAS is the abbreviation for on active service
one's is read as one is, I plus S

explanation.surface: A soldier on active service posted to a desert.
explanation.walkthrough: 'one's' is I (one) plus S for 'is'. The definition describes a place, a fertile spot where travellers stop in the desert.
explanation.definitionFit: A watered fertile spot is where caravans halt and rest among the sands.

clue.text: Leant over, say, for this feast?

definitions.text: Leant over, say, for this feast?

parts.words: Leant over, say, for this feast?
parts.note: leant sounds like Lent, so the clue says that once the fasting season is over this feast arrives

explanation.surface: A puzzle about leaning over at a banquet.
explanation.walkthrough: Lent is the Christian fast of forty days before the spring festival that follows it.
explanation.definitionFit: The Christian spring festival of the Resurrection comes at the close of the Lenten fast.

indicators.note: surprisingly says the letters of steady are rearranged unexpectedly

explanation.surface: Someone was unexpectedly calm.
explanation.definitionFit: To have remained somewhere is to have stopped on there, a past-tense synonym.

parts.note: to mate is to pair up or marry, so wed

explanation.surface: Someone attracted to a partner.
explanation.definitionFit: A car drawn behind another has been pulled along on a rope, a past-participle synonym.

clue.text: Women who only play at work

definitions.text: Women who only play at work

parts.words: Women who only play at work
parts.note: reads like idle women who loaf on the job; really women whose job is performing in plays

explanation.surface: A grumble about female workers who just mess about.
explanation.definitionFit: Stage performers' work consists of playing roles, so playing is their profession.

definitions.meaning: something essential rather than an indulgence

explanation.definitionFit: A requirement is something needed, and an essential item is the opposite of an indulgent extra.

definitions.meaning: to have a sample or brief feel of something, as in a first go
discernment in judging what is fine or elegant

explanation.definitionFit: One may get a brief sample of freedom, and refined judgement in art or dress is good discernment.

indicators.note: changes says the letters of in a team are rearranged

explanation.surface: A manager motivates players by making substitutions in a side.
explanation.walkthrough: 'changes' rearranges the seven letters of IN A TEAM.
explanation.definitionFit: To enliven or spur on someone is to give them spirit, a verb synonym.

parts.note: reads like half-hearted political orders; really a drill order to turn half a full rotation

explanation.surface: An order issued by a half-hearted revolutionary.
explanation.definitionFit: The parade-ground order makes soldiers face the opposite way, a half rotation.

parts.note: D is a musical note
earth is ground or land

explanation.surface: A remark about the shortage of available land.
explanation.definitionFit: A shortage or lack of something is a scarcity, a noun synonym.

parts.note: reads like an arm made of the metal; really the club carried by a British police officer

explanation.surface: An ancient weapon made of copper.
explanation.walkthrough: Copper is British slang for a police officer.
explanation.definitionFit: British police constables carried a short wooden baton as their weapon.

clue.text: Topping sort of plum to take on again

indicators.note: topping means cutting off the top, the first letter of the plum

parts.note: the greengage is a type of green plum

explanation.surface: A fine variety of plum, rehired.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Topping' looks like praise for the plum but means removing its first letter, G, from GREENGAGE.
explanation.definitionFit: To rehire or employ someone once more is to engage them a second time.

clue.text: Enthusiasm found in no western film street

indicators.note: no says a letter is to be dropped from the street name

parts.note: Wardour Street in London's Soho is the home of the British film industry

explanation.surface: Zeal seen in a cinema street that shows no cowboy films.
explanation.walkthrough: 'western' looks like a film genre but gives W, which 'no' removes from WARDOUR, the London street long home to film companies.
explanation.definitionFit: Ardour is passionate zeal, a noun synonym for keenness.

parts.note: a rag is a worn-out, tattered garment
démodé means out of fashion, so out

explanation.surface: An old ragged dress is naturally out of fashion.
explanation.definitionFit: A rich meat stew is served as a dish, one course of a meal.

parts.note: to do someone is to swindle or con them

indicators.note: return means the birds' name is read backwards

parts.note: emus are large flightless birds

explanation.surface: A question whether birds come back to feed.
explanation.walkthrough: 'return' turns EMUS round to SUME, which follows CON.
explanation.definitionFit: To devour food is to consume it, a verb synonym.

clue.text: Bob is short, and yes, rising

parts.note: curt means short or brusque in manner

indicators.note: rising in a down clue means the word yes is read upwards, backwards

explanation.surface: Bob gives a short reply and stands up saying yes.
explanation.walkthrough: 'rising' turns YES upward into SEY, following CURT.
explanation.definitionFit: A bob is a quick bending of the knees as a respectful greeting, a noun synonym.

indicators.note: in puts the abbreviation for pages inside the valley

parts.note: a dale is a valley, a depression in the land

explanation.surface: Pages kept in a low mood become blotchy.
explanation.walkthrough: 'depression' looks like low mood but means a valley, DALE, which takes PP inside.
explanation.definitionFit: Dapple describes a coat marked with patches of colour, as in a dapple-grey horse.

clue.text: Making a point, established an advantage

parts.note: S is a compass point, south
set means fixed or established

explanation.surface: Someone arguing a point and so gaining an edge.
explanation.definitionFit: A benefit or useful resource is an asset, a noun synonym.

clue.text: Sol is back and a little hollow

indicators.note: back means the sun and is are read backwards together

parts.note: Sol is the Latin name for the sun

explanation.surface: Sol is back and there is a small dip.
explanation.walkthrough: 'back' turns SUN IS round to SINUS.
explanation.definitionFit: A cavity in the skull bone is a small hollow space, an anatomical term.

clue.text: Uncommonly long face about right for a high-flier

indicators.note: about puts the scrambled letters around the abbreviation for right
uncommonly means the letters of long face are arranged unusually

explanation.surface: An oddly long-faced person suited to a high-flying career.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Uncommonly' turns LONG FACE into GEFALCON; 'about' wraps it round R after GE.
explanation.definitionFit: The gerfalcon, a large Arctic falcon, soars at height, so it is a bird that flies high.

parts.note: as means like
APH was the signature of the humorist and MP Sir Alan Patrick Herbert

explanation.surface: Someone as good as George Herbert, a holy man.
explanation.walkthrough: A.P. Herbert, British writer and MP, signed his Punch pieces APH. St Asaph founded the Welsh cathedral city that bears his name.
explanation.definitionFit: The sixth-century Welsh bishop is venerated as a holy man of the Church.

clue.text: They may be suspended for good time-keeping!

definitions.text: They may be suspended for good time-keeping!

parts.words: They may be suspended for good time-keeping!
parts.note: reads like workers punished despite being punctual; really swinging weights hung in clocks that keep time

explanation.surface: An ironic note that people get suspended for being punctual.
explanation.definitionFit: Clock weights hung on a rod swing at a steady rate, regulating timekeeping.

parts.note: reads like a betrothal ring; really an enclosure where combatants engage in battle

explanation.surface: A ring given when a couple get engaged.
explanation.definitionFit: An amphitheatre or stadium is the enclosed space where fighters meet in combat.

indicators.note: Some says the answer is a run of letters hidden inside the words that follow

parts.note: the letters run across the end of one word into the next

explanation.surface: A description of a restless, lively elderly Jewish man.
explanation.definitionFit: The members of an ascetic sect in Judea around the time of Christ were Jews of antiquity.

clue.text: "A fool must now and then be right, — " (Cowper)

definitions.text: "A fool must now and then be right, — " (Cowper)

parts.words: A fool must now and then be right
parts.note: a line from William Cowper's poem Conversation, with the closing two words left blank to be supplied

explanation.surface: A quotation from the poet Cowper with its last words missing.
explanation.definitionFit: The line completes as accidentally, a fool being right only through luck.
